agent.problem: David appears for the first time without any simple identification of who he is. The opening should introduce him, not merely call this a psalm of David.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

agent.problem: The blank asks for the unseen BSB verb in "the LORD ___ His anointed." This makes the baker supply the next wording of a line from a verse that has not yet been told, rather than testing a meaning already established by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The walkthrough never tells the first petition of Psalm 20:9: the direct request for the LORD to save the king. Card 15 only establishes that the person is the king, and this card covers only the request to answer us, leaving the closing petition incomplete.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: The second sentence also retells the opening petition from Psalm 20:1, but the card cites only Psalm 20:9. The citation therefore does not cover all the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
